# Route table snapshot

<!-- generated by: sierra routes --config config/sierra.config.js -->

Generated from `src/routes` by `sierra routes`. **Do not edit.**

A route table is a naming convention over a file tree — a rename moves a URL,
a `_module.mesa` one directory up rewraps every page beneath it, and nothing
in the app refers to either by name. Regenerate after moving a file and read
the diff: a URL that changed without a change you meant to make is a link
somebody else already published.

```
10 routes · 1 layout · target spa · trailing slash always
```

## Routes

`Layout` is the `_module.mesa` the scanner resolved — the nearest one up the
tree, unless the page declared `reset`. Params are the URL's own; the meta
column is what the page DECLARED, already merged down the layout chain.

## Declared meta

Frontmatter, `.meta.js` companion and inherited layout meta, merged the way
the router merges them — layout, then companion, then the page's own. A key
arriving from a layout appears on every page under it, which is the change
this section exists to show.
